comment: Every expected value below was computed by an independent SQL query against
data/sports.db, never taken from the model's answer. The `groundTruthSql` field records
the query used, so a reviewer can re-derive any number here in one paste.
Goldens are grouped by the failure class they defend against. Several exist specifically
because the recorded model gets them wrong.

goldens.question: How many teams are in the database?
goldens.rationale: Sanity check that the happy path works. Note teams is one row per school per sport, so 16 teams across 10 schools.

goldens.question: What is Derek Foss's total passing yards?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT SUM(pass_yds) FROM player_game_stats WHERE player_id = 37;
goldens.rationale: The model's SQL is right here. Proves the validation layer does not over-block correct work.

goldens.question: How many players are on the Oak Hill football roster?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM players p JOIN teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id WHERE t.school = 'Oak Hill' AND t.sport = 'Football';
goldens.rationale: Roster count must include the 4 positions that have no stat rows. Counting distinct players in player_game_stats would give the wrong answer.

goldens.question: How many games did Jackson Prep win in the 2025 football season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN (home_team_id=1 AND home_score>away_score) OR (away_team_id=1 AND away_score>home_score) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM games WHERE 1 IN (home_team_id, away_team_id);
goldens.rationale: Jackson Prep football played 8 games and won 3. Requires checking both home and away orientations.

goldens.question: How many touchdowns did Tony Jackson score this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT SUM(td) FROM player_game_stats WHERE player_id = 14;
goldens.rationale: The model emits SUM(s.touchdowns); the column is td. Must answer 15 rather than surfacing a SQLite error.

goldens.question: How many total points has Marcus Bell scored this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT SUM(s.points) FROM player_game_stats s JOIN games g ON g.game_id = s.game_id WHERE s.player_id = 113;
goldens.rationale: player_season_totals says 165 across 7 games; the fact table says 232 across 9. The rollup's updated_at is 2026-02-10 but the season ran to 2026-02-24. A regression to 165 must fail this golden.

goldens.question: What was Marcus Bell's average points per game this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT SUM(s.points)*1.0/COUNT(DISTINCT s.game_id) FROM player_game_stats s JOIN games g ON g.game_id = s.game_id WHERE s.player_id = 113;
goldens.rationale: 232/9 = 25.78. The rollup would give 165/7 = 23.57. Also guards against integer division.

goldens.question: Who scored the most points in basketball during the 2025-26 season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT p.first_name||' '||p.last_name, SUM(s.points) FROM player_game_stats s JOIN games g ON g.game_id=s.game_id JOIN players p ON p.player_id=s.player_id WHERE g.sport='Basketball' GROUP BY s.player_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1;
goldens.rationale: Marcus Bell leads with 232 despite playing only 9 games. Correct only when computed from the fact table.

goldens.question: Who had the most rebounds in a single game?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM player_game_stats WHERE rebounds = (SELECT MAX(rebounds) FROM player_game_stats);
goldens.rationale: Twelve stat lines tie at 12 rebounds. The model's ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 returns one arbitrary name and presents it as fact. Must report the tie.

goldens.question: What was the highest scoring football game?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT home_score+away_score t FROM games WHERE sport='Football' ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 3;
goldens.rationale: Two games tie at 73: Central Valley 38-35 Lakewood and Riverside 35-38 Lakewood. The model returns one, with no team names at all.

goldens.question: How many injuries were reported for Riverside this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='injuries';
goldens.rationale: There is no injuries table. The model still emits SQL against one at confidence 0.88, which is why model confidence cannot be the gate.

goldens.question: Who is the best player?
goldens.rationale: No defensible default. The model asserts best = most total points, which both mixes sports and rewards players on 14-game schedules.

goldens.question: Did Riverside beat Oak Hill this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT g.sport, h.school, g.home_score, a.school, g.away_score FROM games g JOIN teams h ON h.team_id=g.home_team_id JOIN teams a ON a.team_id=g.away_team_id WHERE (h.school='Riverside' AND a.school='Oak Hill') OR (h.school='Oak Hill' AND a.school='Riverside');
goldens.rationale: Opposite answers by sport, so a bare yes/no is wrong half the time. The model's SQL also has an unbalanced quote and only checks Riverside as home.

goldens.question: Did Riverside beat Oak Hill this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT h.school, g.home_score, a.school, g.away_score FROM games g JOIN teams h ON h.team_id=g.home_team_id JOIN teams a ON a.team_id=g.away_team_id WHERE g.sport='Football' AND ((h.school='Riverside' AND a.school='Oak Hill') OR (h.school='Oak Hill' AND a.school='Riverside'));
goldens.rationale: Proves the slot layer is load-bearing, not decorative. In football Oak Hill won 24-21, so Riverside did NOT beat them - the opposite of the basketball answer.

goldens.question: Did Riverside beat Oak Hill this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM games g JOIN teams h ON h.team_id=g.home_team_id JOIN teams a ON a.team_id=g.away_team_id WHERE g.sport='Basketball' AND ((h.school='Riverside' AND a.school='Oak Hill') OR (h.school='Oak Hill' AND a.school='Riverside'));
goldens.rationale: The same question, other sport: Riverside won both meetings (100-89 and 79-72). Both rows must come back, including the one where Riverside was away.

goldens.question: How many points did Jackson score this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT 'school', school FROM teams WHERE school LIKE '%Jackson%' UNION ALL SELECT 'city', city FROM teams WHERE city LIKE '%Jackson%' UNION ALL SELECT 'player', last_name FROM players WHERE last_name LIKE '%Jackson%';
goldens.rationale: Jackson is a school, a city and a player surname. The model silently picked the football team.

goldens.question: How many points did Jackson score this season?
goldens.groundTruthSql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN home_team_id=1 THEN home_score ELSE away_score END) FROM games WHERE 1 IN (home_team_id, away_team_id);
goldens.rationale: Once the entity is pinned the answer is definite: Jackson Prep football scored 139 points across 8 games.

goldens.question: Who won the state championship?
goldens.rationale: No playoff or championship structure exists. Must refuse rather than substitute a proxy such as most wins.

goldens.question: How many touchdowns did Tony Jackson score this season?
goldens.rationale: Per-game stat lines are a paid surface. The same question answers 15 for a Subscriber, so this golden pins the authorization boundary rather than the data.

goldens.question: How many teams are in the database?
goldens.rationale: Team-level facts stay public. Guards against the role grant being accidentally over-tightened.
